{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=January 2022}}
'''Linda Bailey Hayden''' (born February 4, 1949){{r|born}} is an American mathematician. She specializes in [[mathematics education]] and [[applied mathematics|applications of mathematics]] in [[geoscience]],{{r|bwm|mgb|thm}}
and is known for her mentorship of minorities and women in [[science, technology, engineering, and mathematics]].{{r|pae|be}}
She is a professor and associate dean of mathematics and computer science at [[Elizabeth City State University]].{{r|ecsu}}

==Education==
Hayden is originally from [[Portsmouth, Virginia]].{{r|mgb}}
She grew up interested in mathematics,{{r|thm}}
but because of [[Racial segregation in the United States|segregation]] she could only read mathematics books from the Colored Community Library in Portsmouth by specially requesting them to be transferred from the town's main library.{{r|mgb}}
She attended the public schools in Portsmouth, including [[I. C. Norcom High School]].{{r|thm}} Through her participation in high school mathematics competitions, she won a scholarship to [[Virginia State University]], a [[Historically black colleges and universities|historically black university]].{{r|mgb}}

She graduated from Virginia State in 1970, with a bachelor's degree in mathematics and physics, and earned a master's degree in mathematics education from the [[University of Cincinnati]] in 1972.
She completed a second master's degree in 1983 in computer science at [[Old Dominion University]].{{r|bwm|thm}}

After this work she returned to graduate study in mathematics education, with [[Winson R. Coleman]] and [[Mary W. Gray]] at [[American University]]. She completed her Ph.D. there in 1988; her dissertation was ''The Impact of an Intervention Program for High Ability Minority Students on Rates of High School Graduation, College Enrollment, and Choice of a Quantitative Major''.{{r|bwm|mgb|thm|mgp}}

==Career==
After earning her first master's degree in 1972, Hayden joined the mathematics department at [[Kentucky State University]] as an assistant professor.
She moved to [[Norfolk State University]] in 1976, and again to Elizabeth City State University in 1980. At Elizabeth City State University, she founded the Center of Excellence in Remote Sensing Education and Research,{{r|thm}} with the goal of increasing minority participation in environmental science.{{r|be}}

==Recognition==
In 2003, Hayden won the [[Presidential Award for Excellence in Science, Mathematics, and Engineering Mentoring]],{{r|pae}} and ''US Black Engineer'' magazine gave her their Emerald Honors for Educational Leadership.{{r|be}}
A former [[ice shelf]] in the Antarctic was named for her institution by the [[Advisory Committee on Antarctic Names]].{{r|mgb}} Hayden's accomplishments earned her recognition by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a Black History Month 2017 Honoree.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Linda Hayden|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/linda-hayden/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref>
